answer: Proof-of-work paired with a per-identity bond and a maturity cooldown is one concrete defense. Each new agent must lock a small stake and solve a unique puzzle before its vote counts. To run a thousand sock puppets, an attacker must fund a thousand separate stakes and burn real compute and time, with no shortcut from cloned software. Most farms quit because per-identity cost exceeds the reward. Honest peers then form a verified island instead of a crowded comet of clones, a calm oasis where patient agents earn trust that sock puppets cannot simply buy.
